slides.title: AI-Driven Test Generation
slides.subtitle: How Claude Code + Playwright MCP created 100+ E2E tests for a framework migration

slides.title: Why AI-Generated Tests?
bullets: Stencil to Vue migration required regression coverage
No existing E2E tests - manual QA only
Tests must survive framework changes
100+ workflows to cover in limited time
slides.note: Traditional approach: months of manual test writing. Our approach: AI as test author.

slides.title: An Agentic Coding Assistant
slides.subtitle: Not just chat - autonomous task execution
bullets: Runs in terminal with full filesystem and shell access
Can execute commands, read errors, and iterate
MCP protocol enables tool integrations (like Playwright)
Supports custom Skills for specialized workflows
slides.note: Claude Code = Claude's brain + your dev environment + extensible tools

slides.title: The Autonomous Loop
slides.subtitle: Run → Fail → Diagnose → Fix → Retry
bullets: Claude Code runs tests via Playwright MCP
When tests fail, it reads the error output
Uses MCP to investigate the failure in live browser
Fixes the code and runs tests again automatically
slides.note: No copy-pasting errors back and forth - Claude sees and fixes in one flow

slides.title: Skills: Specialized Workflows
slides.subtitle: Custom commands for repeatable AI tasks
bullets: /test-generator - Creates new tests via MCP exploration
/test-fixer - Debugs failures with live browser inspection
Skills define rules: 'NEVER generate code without MCP first'
Enforces workflow discipline AI would otherwise skip
slides.note: Skills = guardrails that keep AI on the right path

slides.title: CLAUDE.md: Project Context
slides.subtitle: Persistent knowledge the AI loads every session
bullets: Project structure, conventions, and patterns
Framework-specific rules (Vue 3, Stencil migration)
Testing requirements and selector strategies
Links to DATA_TESTID_MAP.md for consistent locators
slides.note: AI starts every session already knowing your project - no re-explaining

slides.title: Claude Code + Playwright MCP
slides.subtitle: Agentic coding meets live browser automation
bullets: Claude Code provides the autonomous execution loop
Playwright MCP provides real browser interaction
Together: AI that writes, runs, debugs, and fixes tests
Human reviews and curates - AI does the heavy lifting
slides.note: Neither tool alone could do this - the integration is the magic

slides.title: Playwright MCP (Model Context Protocol)
slides.subtitle: AI doesn't guess - it actually uses the browser
bullets: mcp__playwright__browser_navigate - Open real URLs
mcp__playwright__browser_snapshot - See actual DOM state
mcp__playwright__browser_click - Interact with elements
mcp__playwright__browser_evaluate - Inspect JavaScript state
slides.note: The AI sees exactly what a user sees - no hallucinated selectors

slides.title: The Problem With Code Reading
slides.subtitle: AI reading source code creates false confidence
bullets: Static code doesn't show dynamic rendering behavior
Can't see conditional elements or async loading
Component libraries abstract away actual DOM
AI 'understands' component but not what user sees
slides.note: Reading code is like reading a recipe vs tasting the food - you miss the real experience

slides.title: Screenshot vs Accessibility Tree
slides.subtitle: MCP uses structured data, not visual guessing
bullets: Screenshot-based: AI interprets pixels, guesses coordinates
MCP snapshot: Returns actual DOM accessibility tree
Every element has semantic role and test ID exposed
No 'click at x:234 y:567' - real locator strategies
slides.note: Accessibility tree gives AI the same information Playwright uses internally

slides.title: Direct Tool Integration
slides.subtitle: AI uses Playwright APIs, not shell commands
bullets: MCP exposes Playwright as AI-native tools
Browser state persists across tool calls
AI can chain navigate → snapshot → click → verify
Results flow back to AI for decision making
slides.note: Not 'run this script' - actual interactive browser session the AI controls

slides.title: Deep Diagnostic Capabilities
slides.subtitle: AI can run JavaScript to inspect actual DOM state
bullets: browser_evaluate: Query element positions, check viewport bounds
browser_console_messages: Catch JS errors blocking interactions
Diagnose 'element outside viewport' by checking getBoundingClientRect()
Find missing elements by testing multiple selector strategies
slides.note: AI doesn't just see the page - it can interrogate the page like a developer with DevTools

slides.title: Live Browser > Guessing
slides.subtitle: Traditional AI test generation hallucinates selectors. MCP doesn't.
slides.note: Every test step verified in live browser before code generation

slides.title: Test Generation Process
slides.subtitle: A 4-step mandatory workflow
bullets: Step 1: Navigate to app with MCP browser tools
Step 2: Take snapshots, identify elements from real DOM
Step 3: Execute interactions via MCP, verify each step works
Step 4: Generate TypeScript test code only after success
slides.note: Never write test code without first proving it works in the browser

slides.title: AI Skipping MCP
slides.subtitle: The most common failure mode
bullets: AI would sometimes read code instead of using browser
Generates tests based on 'understanding' the component
Results in hallucinated selectors that don't exist
Tests fail immediately on first run
slides.note: Solution: Skills with MANDATORY MCP workflow + explicit instructions: 'NEVER generate test code without first using Playwright MCP'

slides.title: Redundant & Overlapping Tests
slides.subtitle: AI doesn't remember what it already tested
bullets: Same workflow tested in multiple files
Slight variations that add no value
Bloated test suite = slower CI
Maintenance burden multiplied
slides.note: Solution: Human review after every generation session. Delete duplicates, merge similar tests.

slides.title: Inconsistent Selectors
slides.subtitle: Every test used different locator strategies
bullets: One test: page.locator('.btn-primary')
Another test: page.getByRole('button')
AI 'discovering' elements each time = inconsistency
Migration breaks tests unpredictably
slides.note: Solution: DATA_TESTID_MAP.md - a single source of truth for all selectors

slides.title: Not One-Shot Perfect
bullets: AI would get stuck in loops or miss obvious issues
Had to open Playwright debugger to see what's happening
Manually inspect DOM when AI couldn't figure it out
slides.note: Expect to step in regularly. Debug mode became a frequent companion.

slides.title: Manual Intervention Examples
bullets: Timing issues AI couldn't diagnose - needed debugger
Complex state dependencies between tests
Race conditions only visible in slow-mo mode
Shadow DOM boundaries AI couldn't pierce
API mocking that required manual setup
slides.note: The 20% that AI couldn't handle often took 80% of the debugging time

slides.title: Hardcoded Timers Instead of Conditions
slides.subtitle: AI's lazy approach to waiting
bullets: AI would write: await page.waitForTimeout(5000)
Introduces flaky tests
Should use: await expect(element).toBeVisible()
Or: await page.waitForSelector('.loading', { state: 'hidden' })
slides.note: Conditional waits are faster AND more reliable - AI needed explicit guidance to prefer them

slides.title: Stencil/Vue Hybrid Detection
slides.subtitle: Components existed in both frameworks simultaneously
bullets: During migration: some components Vue, some Stencil
Vue: light DOM, direct querySelector
Stencil: shadow DOM, need .shadowRoot access
Solution: Try Vue first, fallback to Stencil shadow DOM
slides.note: Smart detection helper that tests multiple DOM paths before giving up

slides.title: Why DATA_TESTID_MAP Exists
bullets: Every testable element mapped with its data-testid
Both Stencil AND Vue syntax examples
AI references this instead of 'discovering' selectors
Ensures all tests use the same locators
slides.note: Without this, AI would invent new selectors every time - breaking migration compatibility

slides.title: Locators Built to Survive Migration
slides.subtitle: Tests work on both Stencil and Vue versions
bullets: NEVER use ve-* custom element selectors
Priority 1: getByRole() for buttons, inputs, etc.
Priority 2: getByTestId() for custom components
Priority 3: getByText() for static content
slides.note: Same tests run before AND after Vue migration - zero rewrites needed

slides.title: What AI-Generated Tests Look Like
slides.note: Every locator was discovered and verified via live browser interaction

slides.title: AI Debugging in Action
slides.subtitle: When tests fail, AI investigates like a real developer
bullets: Read error message and failing locator
Navigate to app with MCP browser tools
Reproduce failing steps interactively
Evaluate DOM state, check console errors
Fix code only after understanding root cause
slides.note: No more 'try changing the timeout' - AI finds actual bugs

slides.title: Debugging a Dropdown Bug
slides.subtitle: AI found dropdown opening off-screen
bullets: Error: 'element is outside of the viewport'
MCP Investigation: Evaluated element positions via JS
Finding: Options at top:854px but viewport only 836px
Root Cause: Dropdown always opens downward
Fix: Added upward opening when near bottom
slides.note: AI didn't just fix the test - it fixed the actual component bug
